newsitem.title: ITALY: Top Italy court annuls antitrust fine on insurers.
newsitem.headline: Top Italy court annuls antitrust fine on insurers.

text.p: Italy's State Council, the country's highest court for administrative justice, annulled a decision by the antitrust body in 1994 to fine major Italian insurance companies billions of lire for violating competition laws.
Italian insurers' association Ania said the state council said there was not enough evidence to show the companies, which include insurer Generali, had anti-competitive accords.
Other firms concerned in the ruling are Fondiaria, Milano, Sai, Ras, Toro, Reale Mutua, Unipol, Assitalia, Lloyd Adriatico and Zurigo.
Following an investigation in 1994, the antitrust authority imposed fines on the companies for a total of some 22 billion lire for setting up a cartel in the non-life insurance sector.

It said at the time the companies, which had 53.3 percent of the non-life insurance market, periodically exchanged information on their business between 1990 and 1993 to reach a common commercial policy.

Last August, the administrative tribunal of the region of Lazio overturned the imposition of the fines by the antitrust authority but said there was convergent tendency on premiums which was capable of altering the market.
The case then went to the State Council.

Ania said the State Council ruled out the idea that "the meetings between company technicians, judged by the antitrust to be real anti-competition agreements, actually constituted accords restricting freedom of competition, a theory which was not sufficiently proven."
